content.text:
This is a single-line diagram of an electrical distribution system. Filled breaker squares are closed; hollow squares are open (N.O. = normally open). Power flows through closed breakers, transformers and conductors in either direction, from the sources at the top. Ignore equipment ratings. Breaker CB-4 trips open; every other breaker stays as drawn. Which loads lose power? Answer with the load names exactly as written on the diagram, as a comma-separated list in any order.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
CB-4 is the only feed to transformer T-3, and T-3 is the only source for MCC-3. Tracing the single-line diagram:

1. **Bus A (13.8 kV)** feeds three branches through CB-2, CB-3 and CB-4.
2. **CB-4** feeds **T-3** (750 kVA, 13.8 kV–480 V), which feeds **MCC-3**.
3. **MCC-3** feeds three breakers: CB-9 (Chlorine Feed), CB-10 (Aeration Blower 3) and CB-11 (Maintenance Shop).
4. MCC-3's bus bar has no tie to MCC-1 or MCC-2, and no other breaker connects it to any other source. The normally open breakers in the diagram are not present, so nothing provides an alternate path.

When CB-4 trips open, T-3 and MCC-3 are de-energized, so all three loads downstream of MCC-3 lose power. The other branches (T-1/MCC-1 and T-2/MCC-2/PNL-1) remain energized through CB-2 and CB-3.

Loads losing power: Chlorine Feed, Aeration Blower 3, Maintenance Shop.

FINAL ANSWER: Chlorine Feed, Aeration Blower 3, Maintenance Shop

Tracing the feed chain: CB-4 supplies T-3, and T-3 feeds MCC-3, which serves CB-9, CB-10, and CB-11. Next I'm checking whether MCC-3 has any other supply path, starting with whether its bus bar connects to anything beyond T-3.

I'm checking the rest of the MCC-3 bus and the other buses for any tie, and I don't see any. MCC-3 is fed only through CB-4, so Chlorine Feed, Aeration Blower 3, and Maintenance Shop would all lose power if that breaker opens.
